subtopics.name: Key points
points: Vegetation is set by altitude + climate (temperature, rainfall) + soil + human activity.
Nepal zones: Terai → Sub-montane → Temperate → Sub-alpine → Alpine → Nival.
Terai: sal forest + grasslands (warm, low rainfall).
Temperate: oak, rhododendron (national flower), chestnut.
Sub-alpine: pine, fir, juniper; Alpine: meadows, dwarf shrubs, lichens.

Dominant species: sal (Terai), rhododendron + oak (temperate), pine + fir (sub-alpine), meadows + lichens…

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Nepal's vegetation is zoned by altitude and climate.
The Terai is dominated by sal forest and grasslands; the temperate hills by rhododendron and oak.
The tree line ends at ~3000–4500 m; alpine vegetation is meadows and dwarf shrubs.

subtopics.name: Exam focus

Zones: Terai → Sub-montane → Temperate → Sub-alpine → Alpine → Nival (rising).
Sal = Terai; Rhododendron + Oak = temperate; Pine + Fir = sub-alpine; Meadows = alpine.

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Vegetation zones are defined by ALTITUDE + climate (rainfall, temperature), not by political boundaries.
Sal (Shorea robusta) is the dominant Terai/subtropical tree; rhododendron dominates the temperate hills.
Burning/shifting agriculture (jhum) degrades vegetation; natural regrowth is slow on poor soils.

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Vegetation conservation: in-situ + ex-situ strategies.
Nepal: community forestry (~36% of forest land) is a global success story.
Threats: jhum, grazing, firewood, logging, climate change, pollution.
